instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: LegalTech startup providing an AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform for SME legal departments. Automating contract review, clause extraction, obligation tracking, and renewal management. 150 customers across Europe. Expanding into regulatory change monitoring with automated contract impact analysis. We are a bootstrapped company with a lean team. Every euro of investment must show near-immediate ROI given our constrained working capital. The founder is involved in all strategic decisions including innovation priorities.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: Our industry is facing structural decline due to technological disruption and changing consumer behavior. We cannot rely on incremental improvements to our legacy business — we need to identify entirely new value propositions that leverage our brand, customer relationships, or operational capabilities in adjacent spaces where demand is growing, not shrinking.
answers.teamSize: We have 2 generalist developers who split their time between maintaining our existing systems, handling customer support escalations, and occasionally prototyping new features. There is no dedicated innovation or R&D role — innovation happens when these developers have spare cycles between urgent operational tasks, which is rare.

input.changes_since_last: Post-merger integration underway. Team doubled to 2 members. Culture clash between legacy and new teams.

opportunities.title: Self-Service Regulatory Compliance Dashboard (Evolved)
opportunities.rationale: Building on the prior attempt, this iteration focuses specifically on regulatory monitoring. By limiting the scope to core compliance dashboards derived from existing contracts, we increase the likelihood of adoption and provide immediate ROI for both user and company.

first_actions: Map 3 high-risk/high-frequency regulations affecting current client base.
Develop a tiered feature set (Basic view -> Alerting System).
Conduct focused interviews with the top 5 'champion' clients to validate workflow integration.
execution_plan.success_metric: Monthly active users of the compliance dashboard (Target: 30% increase in usage vs baseline).
milestones: MVP developed for a single regulatory domain.
Positive feedback loop on alert accuracy.

opportunities.title: Predictive Litigation Risk Scoring Engine (Diversification)
opportunities.rationale: Given the structural decline in traditional legal services, leveraging AI to predict litigation risk based on client interaction data is a radical diversification play. This shifts Synapse from being a reactive platform (reviewing contracts) to a proactive strategic advisor.

first_actions: Identify 3 key data points correlating with litigation history in the legal sector.
Develop initial predictive model using historical client data sets (anonymized).
Prototype a 'Risk Score' output presented alongside contract review findings.
execution_plan.success_metric: Successful demonstration of the Risk Score to a paying client, leading to an upsell opportunity.
milestones: Sales pitch deck incorporating the new service line.

opportunities.title: Cross-Functional Knowledge Sharing Protocol
opportunities.rationale: The culture clash and limited talent pool highlight a structural process gap. Implementing a formalized knowledge exchange mechanism will improve team cohesion, leverage the combined skills of the merged teams, and free up developer cycles.

first_actions: Implement bi-weekly 'Brown Bag' sessions covering both legacy and new operational processes.
Create a simple internal wiki/knowledge base for standardized documentation.
Define clear roles for who owns the updated process documents (e.g., one generalist per function).
execution_plan.success_metric: Completion and adoption of documented processes for the top 3 operational areas.
milestones: Knowledge base launched with minimum viable content.
Scheduled and held first two cross-functional sessions.

next_steps.action: Schedule a dedicated 'Innovation Day' with the founder and key team members to formally scope the Predictive Litigation Risk Scoring Engine.
Develop a formal communication plan addressing the cultural integration gaps, focusing on shared mission and future vision (The 'Why').
Create a simple process map detailing the workflow dependencies between core systems and regulatory monitoring processes.

key_weaknesses: Cultural friction/Integration overhead slowing down development cycles.
Lack of dedicated, protected time for R&D outside of urgent operational support.
Over-reliance on the founder's availability and singular decision-making authority.

improvements: Successfully expanding scope into high-value regulatory change monitoring, increasing service depth.
Demonstrating clear strategic intent to move beyond incremental improvements (diversification focus).
persistent_gaps: Sustained team bandwidth remains fragmented between support and development tasks.
Formal process documentation is still reactive rather than proactive.
achieved_milestones: Completed initial phase of previous recommendation (opp_2), building confidence in the regulatory expansion path.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The assessment shifted focus from general process improvements to specific diversification strategies (regulatory monitoring). The company has increased its perceived strategic ambition and market awareness regarding structural industry decline.
